title: Deterministic fixture corpus with CPU-oracle equivalence checking
description:
A new `dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/` prototype crate carries a deterministic seeded fixture corpus and a CPU-oracle equivalence checker that every arithmetic and kernel candidate in the wave-parallel permanent study is measured against.

## Background

The study compares arithmetic representations and GPU execution mappings for permanents over $\mathbb{F}_3$, $\mathbb{F}_5$, and $\mathbb{F}_7$. No correctness evidence is admissible until a candidate is shown exactly equal to an in-tree CPU oracle on inputs that reach the structural boundaries of the algorithm, not only on uniform random matrices.

The existing measurement harness at `dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/` samples uniform random matrices only. Nothing in the repository constructs matrices or Gray-code indices that target a range boundary, an addition-versus-subtraction transition, a nonzero exponent class, or a zero-containing row product. That corpus is prerequisite infrastructure for the candidate work rather than a rider on any single candidate.

The oracle is `gf2_algebra::permanent::permanent_ryser`, which is field-agnostic and asserts $n \le 63$, so it covers every order the study measures, including orders where no packed $\mathbb{F}_7$ kernel exists. Where a packed scalar kernel supports the order, it serves as a second reference and the reference actually used is recorded per row.

The horizontal product of a row-packed Ryser step reaches its slow path only when no active row sum is zero. For a uniform random matrix and a fixed nonempty column subset the row sums are independent and uniform, so the exact marginal probability is

$$
\Pr[Z=0] = \left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n .
$$

Recording the observed frequency beside that expectation is a diagnostic the corpus has to support.

The crate is also where the study's measurement backends are dispatched from, so it opens with an adapter surface covering every planned prototype path. A path with no implementation behind it yet reports itself unsupported with a stated reason, which is how the existing harness already records a backend it cannot run.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/` exists as a standalone crate outside the Cargo workspace, carrying a `.gitignore` whose entries are `target/` and `Cargo.lock`, and a README stating the crate's scope together with its build and test invocations.
- [hard] REQ-02: A fixture module emits a deterministic corpus keyed by an explicit seed, so that two runs at the same seed produce byte-identical matrices, and the corpus is reproducible from a committed command.
- [hard] REQ-03: The corpus covers, for each of $\mathbb{F}_3$, $\mathbb{F}_5$, and $\mathbb{F}_7$: empty and singleton matrices where the exercised API accepts them, Gray-range boundary indices including the first and last index of a partitioned interval, both addition and subtraction Gray transitions, active-lane masking at partially filled words, zero-containing row products, and each nonzero exponent class of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$.
- [hard] REQ-04: The corpus includes orders $n = 16$, $n = 20$, and $n = 24$ for $\mathbb{F}_7$, spanning the $n \le 16$ bound that the current 16-lane packed $\mathbb{F}_7$ representation imposes.
- [hard] REQ-05: An equivalence checker compares a candidate's per-matrix result element-wise against `gf2_algebra::permanent::permanent_ryser`, reports the count of mismatching matrices together with the first mismatching fixture identifier, and records a candidate that cannot execute with a stated reason instead of dropping it.
- [hard] REQ-06: The checker reports the observed zero-fast-path frequency for each $(q, n)$ cell of the corpus beside the exact marginal expectation $\left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n$.
- [hard] REQ-07: The crate exposes one adapter entry point per planned prototype measurement path, each returning an unsupported result with a stated reason until its implementation lands, so a measurement driver can enumerate the full path set from the start.
- [hard] REQ-08: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/Cargo.toml --release` passes, exercising the corpus against the oracle through the CPU-side reference paths.
- [hard] REQ-09: `cargo fmt --manifest-path dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/Cargo.toml -- --check` and `cargo clippy --manifest-path dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/Cargo.toml --release --all-targets -- -D warnings` report no findings.

## Notes

The crate is excluded from the default workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles it; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocations above are the only build evidence for this change.

Crates under `dev/research/` are permanent repository content, which is what lets rejected candidates and their falsifying evidence stay compiled and tested for the life of the study.

The value-to-exponent tables the exponent-class coverage is drawn from are, with generator $2$ for $\mathbb{F}_5$ and generator $3$ for $\mathbb{F}_7$:

| $\mathbb{F}_5$ value | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $3$ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Exponent | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |

| $\mathbb{F}_7$ value | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $6$ | $4$ | $5$ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Exponent | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |

planning.outcome: A seeded fixture corpus in a new prototype crate reproduces exact CPU-oracle permanents across the study's boundary classes for three fields.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One crate stub plus one fixture module and one oracle comparator, all host-side, verifiable in a single focused cycle without a device.

title: HIP event timing API for device-side kernel spans
description:
A HIP event wrapper in the kernels crate's device host layer, returning the elapsed device time of a kernel span so a measurement can separate kernel execution from allocation, copy, and host serialization.

## Background

Every GPU figure recorded for the permanent kernels so far is a wall-clock span around a whole dispatch: host serialization of the batch, two device allocations, a host-to-device copy, the launch, a device synchronize, a device-to-host copy, and two frees. Kernel-only duration cannot be recovered from it, and no HIP event is used anywhere in `crates/gf2-kernels-hip` today.

Event objects are device resources acquired and released through the HIP FFI, which is the same category as the buffers, streams, and launch dimensions the crate already owns. `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/` exports `DeviceBuffer`, `PinnedHostBuffer`, `HipStream`, `HipStreamPool`, and `LaunchDims`; events belong beside them. A private event helper inside a research crate would duplicate a shared device-resource mechanism, which the repository's convention-convergence rule treats as a defect unless it is a named exception.

This is production `unsafe` in the crate that is permitted to hold it, so each FFI boundary carries its own safety contract.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/` exposes an event type that acquires a HIP event on construction and releases it on drop, with no path that leaks the event on an error return.
- [hard] REQ-02: The API records a start event and a stop event on a caller-supplied stream and returns the elapsed device time between them in milliseconds.
- [hard] REQ-03: Querying elapsed time before the stop event has completed returns a stated error rather than a partially observed duration.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every `unsafe` block the change introduces carries an explicit safety contract naming the precondition it relies on.
- [hard] REQ-05: A device-gated test records a span around a known-duration kernel and asserts the returned duration is positive and bounded by the enclosing wall-clock span.
- [hard] REQ-06: Device-touching tests are gated on the crate's `hip` feature and marked ignored with a reason naming the required device, matching the convention of the crate's existing test files.
- [hard] REQ-07: `cargo test --manifest-path crates/gf2-kernels-hip/Cargo.toml --release --features hip` compiles on a ROCm host, with the device-gated tests reported as ignored when no device is present.

## Notes

`crates/gf2-kernels-hip` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace and requires ROCm, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles it; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

Scope is the event API and its tests. No measurement, receipt, or harness integration belongs here.

planning.outcome: A HIP event wrapper in the kernels crate returns elapsed device time for a kernel span, with a safety contract on each unsafe boundary.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One RAII wrapper over three HIP entry points with its safety contracts is a small self-contained cycle in a crate that already owns device resources.

title: Purpose-domain stream address allocator
description:
A bounded, injective seed-address encoding for the measurement harness, so each measurement purpose addresses the sampler through a distinct region of the seed input space instead of through a hand-chosen numeric base.

## Background

The harness derives a ChaCha20 seed from four little-endian `u64` words — campaign root, field order $q$, matrix order $n$, and a stream index — so distinct tuples address distinct generator states, and a debug assertion already catches a caller sampling one field from another field's stream label.

What the tuple does not encode is *purpose*. Which stream index belongs to which measurement activity is decided by hand-chosen numeric bases: the grid hands cell $i$ the range $1 + i \times 10^5$, and the sustained runs sit at $10^9 + j \times 10^5$. An earlier revision based the sustained runs at $10^6$, commensurate with the grid's allocation; the ranges overlapped in index space and the pooled counts were valid only because no colliding pair happened to share a $(q, n)$ — verified after the fact rather than designed. Two defects of that family corrupted a superseded result set: every sustained run started at the same stream index, so two runs at one $(q, n)$ drew overlapping matrices; and warm-up shared a stream counter with the timed repetitions, so which matrices a cell timed depended on machine speed and the recorded seed did not regenerate the recorded sample.

The study adds several measurement purposes. Minting another base for each by the same arithmetic is how that defect recurs, so the address space is partitioned by construction instead: a purpose tag occupies a fixed high-bit field of the stream word and the stream index occupies the remaining low bits, with both bounds asserted so the two fields cannot overlap.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[campaign root] --> S[32-byte seed]
    B[field order q] --> S
    C[matrix order n] --> S
    D[purpose tag in high bits] --> W[stream word]
    E[bounded stream index in low bits] --> W
    W --> S
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The seed derivation accepts a purpose tag alongside the existing campaign root, field order, matrix order, and stream index, and encodes that tag in a fixed high-bit field of one seed word with the stream index in the remaining low bits of the same word.
- [hard] REQ-02: The encoding asserts both bounds at the call site: a purpose tag at or above the tag field's capacity, or a stream index at or above the index field's capacity, fails loudly rather than aliasing into another purpose's address region.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test establishes that the encoding is injective over the enumerated purpose set and a bounded index range — distinct $(\text{purpose}, \text{index})$ pairs produce distinct seed inputs — so no two purposes can address the same generator state through this API.
- [hard] REQ-04: A committed table of golden derivation vectors fixes the mapping from a stated $(\text{root}, q, n, \text{purpose}, \text{index})$ tuple to its derived seed bytes and to the leading output bytes of the generator opened on that seed, so a change to the encoding fails the test instead of silently re-addressing already-committed receipts.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every measurement purpose the study runs is a named member of one enumerated purpose set, and warm-up is a distinct purpose from the timed repetitions of the same cell, so a recorded seed regenerates exactly the timed sample.
- [hard] REQ-06: Introducing a measurement purpose without giving it a tag fails the purpose-set test rather than defaulting into an existing purpose's address region.
- [hard] REQ-07: Every call site in the harness that previously computed a stream base arithmetically addresses the sampler through this encoding instead, leaving no hand-chosen numeric base in the measurement path.
- [hard] REQ-08: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/Cargo.toml --release` passes.

## Notes

The guarantee established here is over **seed inputs**: distinct purposes and indices encode to distinct addresses, and the golden vectors pin that mapping. It is not a claim that the resulting ChaCha20 output streams are disjoint as sequences — that is a property of the cipher's construction, and no test in this work establishes it. The criteria are worded to keep those two statements apart.

Every crate under `dev/research/` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles them; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

planning.outcome: Each measurement purpose addresses the sampler through a bounded, injective seed encoding, with golden vectors pinning the mapping.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One bit-field encoding with its bounds assertions, an injectivity test, and a golden-vector table is a small self-contained cycle.

title: Harness micro-measurement modes for Gray update and horizontal product
description:
The permanent measurement harness gains a kernel-only timing column, isolated micro-measurements of the dependency-chained Gray update and of the horizontal row product, and the backend registration through which those modes expose the study's prototype paths.

## Background

The study must report kernel-only throughput separately from end-to-end throughput, and must isolate three nested measurement shapes for each arithmetic representation the study measures: one dependency-chained packed add or subtract on the same accumulator; zero-mask detection plus the complete nonzero horizontal reduction; and the full Ryser loop including matrix preparation, Gray initialization, update, product, partial-sum reduction, launch overhead, and transfer overhead.

The harness at `dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/` times the composite campaign hot path as four component phases — generate, evaluate, reduce, store — with no sub-evaluate decomposition and no kernel-only timer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Gray update micro-measurement] --> B[Horizontal product micro-measurement]
    B --> C[End-to-end Ryser cell]
    C --> D[Kernel-only span beside wall-clock span]
```

Each mode is a new measurement purpose, and the harness addresses the sampler by a bounded purpose tag rather than a hand-chosen numeric stream base, so a mode added here takes a tag from the enumerated purpose set instead of minting an address range of its own.

The harness's backend schedule is driven from a single list, so a path registered there is scheduled by both the equivalence check and the timing grid and cannot silently miss a cell. Registration is how these modes expose the paths they can time, so the study's full prototype path set is registered here in one place; a path whose implementation has not landed reports itself unsupported with a stated reason, which is how the harness already records a backend it cannot run.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The harness reports, per timed cell, a kernel-only device duration beside the existing wall-clock duration, and the CSV schema constant carries the new column so a reader can tell the two apart without consulting code.
- [hard] REQ-02: A micro-measurement mode times one dependency-chained packed add or subtract on a single accumulator, reported separately from surrounding loop overhead.
- [hard] REQ-03: A micro-measurement mode times zero-mask detection plus the complete nonzero horizontal reduction, reporting the fast path and the slow path separately where the measured path permits the distinction.
- [hard] REQ-04: Micro-measurement modes reuse the committed warm-up, repetition-count, timed-duration, and censoring policy of the harness protocol module instead of defining a private timing policy, and a censored micro-measurement row states its censoring reason.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each new mode addresses the sampler through a named purpose tag drawn from the harness's enumerated purpose set, with no numeric stream base computed in the mode's own code.
- [hard] REQ-06: Each of the study's planned prototype measurement paths is present in the harness backend schedule, and a path whose implementation has not landed is reported as unsupported with a stated reason rather than omitted from the schedule.
- [hard] REQ-07: The harness usage text describes each new mode together with its arguments.
- [hard] REQ-08: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/Cargo.toml --release` passes.

## Notes

Scope is measurement infrastructure. No campaign receipt is produced here.

Every crate under `dev/research/` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles them; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

planning.outcome: The measurement harness times one dependency-chained Gray step, the horizontal product, and a kernel-only span, each under a named purpose tag.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two micro-measurement modes over an existing protocol module and an existing address encoding, with no receipt to produce, fits one focused cycle.

title: Wave-cooperative intra-matrix Ryser prototype for F_3
description:
A HIP kernel that gives each lane of a wavefront its own contiguous Gray-code interval of a single matrix and reduces only the partial Ryser sums across the wave, for permanents over $\mathbb{F}_3$.

## Background

Every HIP permanent kernel in this repository today launches a one-thread block per matrix and runs the Gray-code Ryser walk sequentially in that thread. On an RDNA2 wavefront of 32 lanes that leaves 31 lanes inactive, and parallelism comes only from having many matrices in flight. An intra-matrix decomposition is the untested alternative: no wave-cooperative permanent kernel exists anywhere in this repository.

The study's execution mapping gives each lane its own contiguous Gray-code interval. One matrix's walk over $[0, 2^n)$ is partitioned into as many contiguous intervals as there are active lanes; each lane owns its complete packed row-sum accumulator in registers for the whole of its interval, reconstructs that accumulator from the column subset encoded by its interval's start index, applies one packed add or subtract per Gray step, and computes its own horizontal row product locally as a reduction over the row lanes inside its own packed words. Nothing is exchanged across the wave except the partial Ryser sums, which are combined in lane-index order so the reduction is scheduling-independent. The outer $(-1)^n$ factor is applied once after that reduction, and grid and block dimensions are a pure function of matrix order, batch size, and the range partition. This is `crates/gf2-algebra/src/permanent/parallel_bipedal3.rs`'s chunk model with lanes in place of rayon workers.

Giving every lane a full accumulator is what the mapping spends to buy wave utilization, so the per-lane register state and the shared column table are budgeted quantities rather than incidental ones. Beyond its packed accumulator each lane carries three scalar `u64` words — the Gray cursor, its interval end bound, and its partial Ryser sum — so the live per-lane state is the packed word count plus three. The packed column table is staged once per block from global memory by a cooperative strided copy followed by one barrier, and is read-only thereafter. Its steady-state access is **not** a broadcast: at each Gray step a lane reads the column bundle indexed by its own flip index, and flip indices differ across lanes, so shared-memory bank behaviour under that scattered read is a measured quantity rather than an assumption.

That register and shared-memory budget is the central occupancy hypothesis of the study. A packed accumulator holds a fixed number of words for any order the mapping supports, where a byte-oriented accumulator grows with $n$ and will reach scratch memory; each block additionally reserves a column table linear in $n$. Whether that budget, instruction scheduling, or the scattered shared-memory read is what limits occupancy is settled by each field's measurements, not by the estimate stated here.

That CPU precedent partitions the Gray-code index range into fixed-size chunks, reconstructs each chunk's starting column sums from `gf2_algebra::gray::gray_code_index_to_subset`, reduces the partial sums order-independently because addition over $\mathbb{F}_3$ is commutative and associative, and applies the outer factor once after the reduction.

For $\mathbb{F}_3$ the owned per-lane state is one `(magnitude, sign)` `u64` pair, so the live per-lane budget is $2 + 3 = 5$ words of 64 bits, or 10 registers of 32 bits, at every order the mapping supports. The shared read-only column table is two `u64` words per column, so a block reserves $16n$ bytes of shared memory: $384$ bytes at $n = 24$ and $512$ bytes at $n = 32$. $\mathbb{F}_3$ is the field to prototype first because that state is already bit-sliced on the GPU, so the execution mapping can be studied without an arithmetic change confounding it, and because its budget is the floor the other fields are measured against.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Gray-code range of one matrix] --> B[Contiguous interval per lane]
    B --> C[Lane-local accumulator initialized from interval start]
    C --> D[Lane-local packed add or subtract per Gray step]
    D --> E[Lane-local horizontal row product]
    E --> F[Lane-local partial Ryser sum]
    F --> G[Lane-index-ordered partial-sum reduction across the wave]
    G --> H[Outer sign factor applied once]
```

Launch geometry in this repository is a pure function of problem size. A runtime occupancy query would make the launch shape depend on device state and break the pipeline's determinism contract.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A HIP kernel in `dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/` assigns each active lane a contiguous, disjoint Gray-code index interval of one matrix's walk over $[0, 2^n)$, and the intervals together cover that walk exactly once.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each lane holds its own complete `(magnitude, sign)` packed row-sum accumulator in registers for the whole of its interval, and initializes it from the column subset encoded by its interval start index using the index-to-subset semantics of `gf2_algebra::gray::gray_code_index_to_subset`, instead of replaying the walk from index zero.
- [hard] REQ-03: The packed column table is staged once per block in shared memory by a cooperative strided copy followed by one barrier, and is read without modification by every lane of that block thereafter.
- [hard] REQ-04: The kernel documents its per-lane register budget and its per-block shared-memory allocation as functions of matrix order, and the compiler's resource-usage output for the built kernel is committed beside that statement so the two can be compared.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each lane computes its own horizontal row product locally at each Gray step, as a reduction over the row lanes inside its own packed words, with no cross-lane exchange in the product path.
- [hard] REQ-06: Partial Ryser sums are the only quantity reduced across the wave, combined in lane-index order so repeated launches at the same input return an identical result.
- [hard] REQ-07: The outer $(-1)^n$ factor is applied once to the reduced sum.
- [hard] REQ-08: Grid and block dimensions are computed from matrix order, batch size, and the range partition alone, with no runtime occupancy query or device-state probe anywhere in the launch path.
- [hard] REQ-09: The kernel's results are element-wise equal to `gf2_algebra::permanent::permanent_ryser` on the committed fixture corpus in `dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/src/fixtures.rs`, including interval boundary indices, both Gray transition directions, and active-lane masking at partially filled words.
- [hard] REQ-10: The partition, interval initialization, product locality, and partial-sum reduction are exposed as field-parametric surfaces, so a different packed arithmetic instantiates the same mapping without a second partition implementation.
- [hard] REQ-11: Device-touching tests are gated on the crate's device feature and marked ignored with a reason naming the required device, matching the convention of the in-tree HIP test files.
- [hard] REQ-12: `cargo test --manifest-path dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/Cargo.toml --release` passes on a host with no device, and the device-gated equivalence run is recorded as passing on a ROCm host.

## Notes

The prototype crate sits outside the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles it; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

The $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic background is [Scheinerman2024]. The two-plane encoding is a Boolean encoding of $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic, not a field embedding into $\mathbb{F}_2$.

planning.outcome: Each lane walks its own Gray-code interval and only partial Ryser sums cross the wave, matching the CPU oracle over F_3.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One kernel over an already-bit-sliced arithmetic, checked against a corpus that already exists, keeps the cycle to the execution mapping alone.

title: F_3 zero-mask sign-popcount fold candidate beside the halving control
description:
Two executable $\mathbb{F}_3$ horizontal folds under one execution mapping: the current six-stage halving fold as the control, and a candidate that detects a zero row sum with one active-lane mask and reduces the sign product by population count.

- [hard] REQ-03: Both folds return results element-wise equal to `gf2_algebra::permanent::permanent_ryser` on the committed fixture corpus, including zero-containing row products and active-lane masking at partially filled words.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each fold states what it adds to the kernel's per-lane register budget over the five 64-bit words the $\mathbb{F}_3$ mapping already carries, and the compiler's resource-usage output for both built kernels is committed beside those statements, naming registers per thread, private scratch memory per thread, shared memory per block, and spill counts.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each fold is selectable through the crate's measurement path adapter, so a measurement driver can address either without a rebuild.

title: F_5 three-plane accumulator prototype beside the byte-arithmetic control
description:
Two executable $\mathbb{F}_5$ arithmetic paths for the permanent hot path under one execution mapping: the byte-oriented modular arithmetic the shipped GPU kernel uses, and a canonical three-plane accumulator whose horizontal product is a zero mask followed by a $C_4$ log-population-count reduction.

## Background

The current $\mathbb{F}_5$ HIP permanent kernel keeps byte arrays for the matrix columns and for the running column sums, and executes explicit $O(n)$ update and product loops per Gray step. The CPU side is different: `permanent_bipedal5` already runs a packed three-plane path with one constant-time packed add or subtract per Gray step, followed by a horizontal fold that decodes lane by lane and multiplies $\mathbb{F}_5$ elements in a serial loop. The candidate under test replaces that serial fold.

Let `active` hold bits $0,\dots,n-1$ and let $(b_0, b_1, b_2)$ be the canonical value planes. The active zero mask is

$$
Z = \neg(b_0 \lor b_1 \lor b_2) \land \text{active}.
$$

Whether that budget, instruction scheduling, or the scattered shared-memory read is what limits occupancy is settled by each field's measurements, not by the estimate stated here.

The two paths differ sharply in what they cost a lane, and that difference is the occupancy hypothesis this field tests. title: F_3 preregistered receipt campaign
description:
One preregistered measurement campaign over $\mathbb{F}_3$, producing the committed receipts that compare the current GPU path, every planned prototype path that executes on the target device, and the best applicable in-tree CPU path.

## Background

Representation and execution-mapping decisions in this study are settled by receipts rather than by argument. A comparison is sound only when each path in it runs against one identical matrix corpus under one protocol, on an uncontended host, with the provenance needed to reproduce it.

These measurements are what decide which candidates the study keeps, so the campaign's scope is the full planned candidate set for this field, not a pre-filtered one. A candidate that fails to build, fails equivalence, or exhausts a device resource is excluded from the timing comparison and carries that falsifying evidence into the record; a candidate that runs is measured.

Prior measurement over $\mathbb{F}_3$ put no single path ahead across the grid: batch rayon led at $n = 12$, the GPU at batch size $1024$ led from $n = 16$ through $n = 24$, and intra-matrix rayon led at $n = 28$, where the GPU's edge had decayed to $0.984\times$ and no ordering was asserted. The headline of an earlier receipt — a $28.65\times$ GPU win at $n = 24$ — was restated as $0.46\times$ once the baseline was the best CPU path rather than the single-threaded AVX2 one. Those are the figures this campaign has to improve on or confirm.

$\mathbb{F}_3$ also has the smallest zero fast-path share of the three fields, so the fold comparison it carries is the one least likely to be decided by an early return.

The measurement harness at `dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/` already encodes the protocol: an untimed warm-up of at least $3$ s per cell; repetitions until both at least $5$ repetitions and at least $5$ s of timed work have accumulated; a $120$ s cap per cell that censors rather than truncates; a batch size calibrated per cell from a single-matrix probe to target a $2$ s repetition and capped at $65\,536$; matrices drawn by exact rejection from ChaCha20 on structurally disjoint per-purpose stream domains; and a generated provenance preamble carrying binary hash, CPU model, GPU model, and ROCm version.

Timings must separate the kernel-only device span from the surrounding work, because the shipped dispatcher performs host serialization, two device allocations, a host-to-device copy, a launch, a device synchronize, a device-to-host copy, and two frees per call, with no persistent buffers and no streams.

The study's lane-owns-interval mapping gives every lane a full packed accumulator plus three scalar `u64` words, and reserves a shared column table per block that grows with matrix order. That register and shared-memory budget is the study's central occupancy hypothesis: the kernels under measurement each state the budget their design predicts, and this campaign is where the prediction meets the compiler and the device. Reporting the measured figures against the predicted ones is what turns the hypothesis into evidence, in either direction.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Committed receipts compare, over $\mathbb{F}_3$, the current GPU path, every planned prototype path that executes on the target device, and the best applicable in-tree CPU path, with one identical matrix corpus per comparison.
- [hard] REQ-02: Receipts record matrix order, batch size, seed, purpose tag, kernel-only throughput, end-to-end throughput, launch duration, git revision, CPU model, GPU model, ROCm version, compiler version, and each censoring or failure observation.
- [hard] REQ-03: Committed receipts isolate the dependency-chained Gray update, the horizontal product, and the end-to-end Ryser loop for every representation of this field that executes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Receipts cover the current one-thread-per-matrix execution mapping as the control and the lane-owns-interval mapping, at matching orders and batch sizes, so the two mappings are comparable.
- [hard] REQ-05: Event-timed kernel duration is reported in its own column, separate from allocation, copy, and host-serialization time.
- [hard] REQ-06: For each measured kernel of this field, receipts report the registers per thread, private scratch memory per thread, shared memory per block, and spill counts the device actually reported, each beside the per-lane register budget and per-block shared-memory allocation that kernel's design predicted, so a divergence between prediction and measurement is visible rather than inferred.
- [hard] REQ-07: Receipts name the resource that limits occupancy for each measured kernel at each measured order, attributed to the compiler or profiler output that produced the figure.
- [hard] REQ-08: A measurement that contradicts the predicted register or shared-memory budget is recorded together with the contradiction, and the prediction it falsifies is not silently restated.
- [hard] REQ-09: Receipts report the observed zero-fast-path frequency beside the exact marginal expectation $\left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n$ at each measured order, for $q = 3$.
- [hard] REQ-10: Equivalence between each measured path and the CPU oracle is re-confirmed on the campaign host before any timing from the same run counts as evidence, and that confirmation is committed alongside the timing receipts.
- [hard] REQ-11: A censored cell states its censoring reason and the rate it was projected from, and carries no measured throughput value.
- [hard] REQ-12: A planned candidate for this field that cannot execute on the target device is named in the record together with its compile, correctness, or resource falsification, and its exclusion from the timing comparison cites that evidence.
- [hard] REQ-13: The receipts state, for the best-performing prototype at its best operating point, the measured ratio against the best applicable in-tree CPU path and the launch duration at that point.
- [hard] REQ-14: Receipts are reproducible from committed commands, and the campaign runs on the prepared benchmark host under the repository's benchmark lock.

## Notes

Scope is execution and receipts over this one field. Timing instrumentation, prototype kernels, and the harness backend schedule are inputs to this campaign rather than deliverables of it.

The $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic background is [Scheinerman2024].

Receipts belong in the issue's resolved study directory and are attached to the issue as documents rather than referenced by an inline path from another description.

title: F_7 preregistered receipt campaign with bit-plane resource accounting
description:
One preregistered measurement campaign over $\mathbb{F}_7$, producing the committed receipts that compare the current GPU path, every planned prototype path that executes on the target device, and the best applicable in-tree CPU path.

## Background

Representation and execution-mapping decisions in this study are settled by receipts rather than by argument. A comparison is sound only when each path in it runs against one identical matrix corpus under one protocol, on an uncontended host, with the provenance needed to reproduce it.

These measurements are what decide which candidates the study keeps, so the campaign's scope is the full planned candidate set for this field, not a pre-filtered one. A candidate that fails to build, fails equivalence, or exhausts a device resource is excluded from the timing comparison and carries that falsifying evidence into the record; a candidate that runs is measured.

Prior measurement over $\mathbb{F}_7$ put batch rayon on the CPU roughly $3\times$ ahead of the current GPU path at every shared order, and four GPU cells at $n \in \{24, 28\}$ were censored against the $120$ s cap rather than measured. Above $n = 16$ there is no packed CPU kernel at all, so the best applicable in-tree CPU path at those orders is the field-agnostic Ryser driver.

This field carries an extra obligation the other two do not. A bit-sliced $\mathbb{F}_7$ path that executes has to demonstrate exact operation above the current $n \le 16$ lane limit and report what that representation costs in the assembled kernel: bit-plane preparation, register pressure, spills, and achieved occupancy. Those figures are this campaign's to produce for $\mathbb{F}_7$; the study's device-wide qualification consumes them rather than re-measuring them.

The measurement harness at `dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/` already encodes the protocol: an untimed warm-up of at least $3$ s per cell; repetitions until both at least $5$ repetitions and at least $5$ s of timed work have accumulated; a $120$ s cap per cell that censors rather than truncates; a batch size calibrated per cell from a single-matrix probe to target a $2$ s repetition and capped at $65\,536$; matrices drawn by exact rejection from ChaCha20 on structurally disjoint per-purpose stream domains; and a generated provenance preamble carrying binary hash, CPU model, GPU model, and ROCm version.

Timings must separate the kernel-only device span from the surrounding work, because the shipped dispatcher performs host serialization, two device allocations, a host-to-device copy, a launch, a device synchronize, a device-to-host copy, and two frees per call, with no persistent buffers and no streams.

The study's lane-owns-interval mapping gives every lane a full packed accumulator plus three scalar `u64` words, and reserves a shared column table per block that grows with matrix order. That register and shared-memory budget is the study's central occupancy hypothesis: the kernels under measurement each state the budget their design predicts, and this campaign is where the prediction meets the compiler and the device. Reporting the measured figures against the predicted ones is what turns the hypothesis into evidence, in either direction.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Committed receipts compare, over $\mathbb{F}_7$, the current GPU path, every planned prototype path that executes on the target device, and the best applicable in-tree CPU path, with one identical matrix corpus per comparison.
- [hard] REQ-02: Receipts record matrix order, batch size, seed, purpose tag, kernel-only throughput, end-to-end throughput, launch duration, git revision, CPU model, GPU model, ROCm version, compiler version, and each censoring or failure observation.
- [hard] REQ-03: Committed receipts isolate the dependency-chained Gray update, the horizontal product, and the end-to-end Ryser loop for every representation of this field that executes.
- [hard] REQ-04: Receipts cover the current one-thread-per-matrix execution mapping as the control and the lane-owns-interval mapping, at matching orders and batch sizes, so the two mappings are comparable.
- [hard] REQ-05: Event-timed kernel duration is reported in its own column, separate from allocation, copy, and host-serialization time.
- [hard] REQ-06: For each measured kernel of this field, receipts report the registers per thread, private scratch memory per thread, shared memory per block, and spill counts the device actually reported, each beside the per-lane register budget and per-block shared-memory allocation that kernel's design predicted, so a divergence between prediction and measurement is visible rather than inferred.
- [hard] REQ-07: Receipts name the resource that limits occupancy for each measured kernel at each measured order, attributed to the compiler or profiler output that produced the figure.
- [hard] REQ-08: A measurement that contradicts the predicted register or shared-memory budget is recorded together with the contradiction, and the prediction it falsifies is not silently restated.
- [hard] REQ-09: Receipts report the observed zero-fast-path frequency beside the exact marginal expectation $\left(\frac{q-1}{q}\right)^n$ at each measured order, for $q = 7$.
- [hard] REQ-10: Equivalence between each measured path and the CPU oracle is re-confirmed on the campaign host before any timing from the same run counts as evidence, and that confirmation is committed alongside the timing receipts.
- [hard] REQ-11: A censored cell states its censoring reason and the rate it was projected from, and carries no measured throughput value.
- [hard] REQ-12: A planned candidate for this field that cannot execute on the target device is named in the record together with its compile, correctness, or resource falsification, and its exclusion from the timing comparison cites that evidence.
- [hard] REQ-13: The receipts state, for the best-performing prototype at its best operating point, the measured ratio against the best applicable in-tree CPU path and the launch duration at that point.
- [hard] REQ-14: Receipts are reproducible from committed commands, and the campaign runs on the prepared benchmark host under the repository's benchmark lock.
- [hard] REQ-15: Receipts report measured bit-plane input preparation cost separately from the Gray walk, distinguishing the host-side portion from any device-side portion, for every bit-sliced path that executes.
- [hard] REQ-16: Receipts report achieved occupancy for each measured $\mathbb{F}_7$ kernel, attributed to the profiler or compiler output that produced it, beside the occupancy that kernel's stated register and shared-memory budget predicts.
- [hard] REQ-17: Every bit-sliced path that executes is measured at orders $n = 16$, $n = 20$, and $n = 24$, demonstrating exact operation above the current sixteen-lane limit at measurement scale.

## Notes

Scope is execution and receipts over this one field. Timing instrumentation, prototype kernels, and the harness backend schedule are inputs to this campaign rather than deliverables of it.

The $\mathbb{F}_7$ arithmetic background is [Scheinerman2024].

Receipts belong in the issue's resolved study directory and are attached to the issue as documents rather than referenced by an inline path from another description.

title: Runtime qualification of wave utilization and launch duration
description:
A bounded qualification receipt across the study's retained GPU permanent paths: wave utilization, the occupancy-limiting resource, transfer and launch overhead, sustained-kernel duration, and watchdog-safe per-launch work bounds re-derived by measurement.

## Background

A go decision needs to know not only how fast a kernel runs but what the device is doing while it runs, and how long a single launch may safely last. Neither has been measured for any permanent kernel in this repository: no occupancy, register-count, spill, or profiler record for these kernels exists anywhere in the tree.

The watchdog record is contested and has to be treated as such. A prior calibration placed a hang boundary at roughly $190$–$200$ s per launch and derived per-field work budgets on $\text{sub\_batch} \cdot 2^n$ of $4.0 \times 10^9$ at $q = 3$, $1.3 \times 10^9$ at $q = 5$, and $3.5 \times 10^8$ at $q = 7$, with a $400$ ms host cooldown, and recorded that the $\mathbb{F}_3$ kernel never tripped it even on a $2300$ s single launch at $n = 32$. A later observation recorded one device hang and explicitly retracted the attribution of that hang to a watchdog timeout, because no diagnostic separated the possible causes. The safe launch bound reported here therefore comes from this study's own measurement, citing the earlier calibration as a prior rather than as an established device property.

Per-kernel resource figures are produced by each field's own measurement campaign, which reports them against the per-lane register budget and per-block shared-memory allocation that kernel's design predicted. This qualification consumes those committed figures rather than re-measuring them, and adds what no single field can settle: whether that register and shared-memory budget is what limits occupancy across the study's kernels, or whether instruction scheduling, the scattered shared-memory read of the column table, or something else dominates. That is the study's central occupancy hypothesis, and this is where it is answered device-wide.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed receipt reports, for each retained GPU permanent path, the wave utilization achieved by its execution mapping, expressed as the share of wavefront lanes performing useful work.
- [hard] REQ-02: The receipt reports the occupancy-limiting resource for each retained path, together with registers per thread, private scratch memory per thread, shared memory per block, and spill counts; figures already committed by a field's own measurement campaign are cited to their receipt rather than re-measured, and the citation names the file.
- [hard] REQ-03: The receipt states, across the study's kernels, whether the per-lane register budget and per-block shared-memory allocation of the lane-owns-interval mapping is what limits occupancy, naming the resource that does limit it where the answer is no, and citing the measurement behind the verdict.
- [hard] REQ-04: The receipt reports host-to-device transfer time, device-to-host transfer time, and launch overhead, each separate from kernel execution time.
- [hard] REQ-05: The receipt reports sustained-kernel duration as a function of matrix order and per-launch work, measured on the target device.
- [hard] REQ-06: A watchdog-safe per-launch work bound is derived from this study's own measurements for each field, stated together with the measurement that supports it, and reconciled against the earlier calibration figures and the retracted hang attribution described in the background.
- [hard] REQ-07: A measurement that contradicts the earlier calibration, or the register and shared-memory budget the mapping predicted, is recorded together with the contradiction rather than replacing it silently.
- [hard] REQ-08: The qualification is reproducible from committed commands on the prepared benchmark host, under the repository's benchmark lock.

## Notes

Scope is device-wide runtime qualification. The architecture-scope statement and its compile evidence are a separate deliverable, and this qualification makes no claim about architectures beyond the one it measured on.

Committed evidence belongs in the issue's resolved study directory and is attached to the issue as a document rather than referenced by an inline path from another description.

title: Architecture scope statement with compile evidence
description:
The supported GPU architecture set for the study's prototype kernels, stated explicitly and backed by committed compile evidence for each architecture claimed.

## Background

The architecture scope of the permanent kernels is narrower than the repository's target list suggests. The production kernels are compiled with a single unconditional offload architecture, `gfx1030`. A separate per-architecture code-object pipeline exists and records what compiled through a build manifest consumed by the crate's architecture type, but its only sources today are generated no-op probes, and the generated code-object directory is not tracked in the repository.

A claim of support for an architecture is therefore only as good as the compile evidence behind it. The honest floor for the study is the one architecture its kernels are actually built for; widening that set means adding offload-architecture flags to the prototype crate's build and committing what each build produced.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The prototype crate's build accepts an explicit set of offload architectures, defaulting to the single architecture the study measured on, so the compiled set is a stated input rather than an incidental one.
- [hard] REQ-02: A committed artifact records, for each architecture in that set, the compiler invocation and its outcome for every prototype kernel the study retained.
- [hard] REQ-03: A committed statement names the supported GPU architecture scope for the study's kernels, and every architecture it names has compile evidence in that artifact.
- [hard] REQ-04: An architecture that fails to compile is recorded with its failure output and excluded from the supported set, rather than dropped silently.
- [hard] REQ-05: The prototype crate's README states the supported architecture set together with the command that regenerates the compile evidence.
- [hard] REQ-06: `cargo build --manifest-path dev/research/permanent_wave_gpu/Cargo.toml --release` passes on a ROCm host for the default architecture set.

## Notes

Scope is compile-time architecture evidence. Runtime behaviour on any architecture beyond the measured one is outside this work, and the statement says so.

The prototype crate sits outside the default Cargo workspace, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles it; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

title: Field-by-field go/no-go synthesis with production design
description:
The study's findings document: a per-field go or no-go verdict grounded in the committed receipts, a production design behind every go, the validity argument for the $\mathbb{F}_3$ Boolean representation, and the decision on where a permanent-specialized representation lives.

## Background

The study concludes per field, and a no-go is a legitimate conclusion where reproducible evidence does not support GPU acceleration. A go decision requires exact equivalence, reproducible receipts, a safe launch duration, and an end-to-end crossover against the best applicable in-tree CPU path; a win on an isolated operator is insufficient.

Three design questions have to be settled in the same document.

The $\mathbb{F}_3$ packed representation encodes a lane as a magnitude bit and a sign bit, with the sign a don't-care when the magnitude is zero. $\mathbb{F}_3$ receives two simultaneous algebraic advantages: $3 = 2^2 - 1$, so Mersenne-style addition is cheap, and $|\mathbb{F}_3^*| = 2$, so the only nonzero distinction is sign. Neither holds for $\mathbb{F}_5^*$ of order four nor for $\mathbb{F}_7^*$ of order six. The document must explain why this is a Boolean encoding of $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic rather than the permanent of a matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

A production design converges on the repository's existing device infrastructure rather than growing a parallel one. Persistent device buffers, pinned host buffers, streams, a stream pool, and launch-dimension types already exist and are public in `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/`; the permanent dispatcher bypasses them today, allocating and freeing per call. The dispatcher also asserts on every device return code and panics, where the repository's accelerator contract requires unsupported capabilities and recoverable resource failures to select a tested fallback while fatal device failures stay explicit.

The representation boundary has exactly two compliant resolutions: change the canonical public packed $\mathbb{F}_7$ representation at its source once broader evidence supports it, or keep the public representation as it is and define the three-plane state as an internal permanent-kernel representation with explicit scope, shared behavioral tests, and a tracked convergence condition. A public packed representation also attracts a proof obligation by repository convention, which an internal permanent-kernel state does not obviously attract.

An archived encoding decision rejected a three-plane $\mathbb{F}_7$ candidate under a workload model weighting each Gray transition as one packed add or subtract plus roughly $n-1$ packed multiplications, and states that a re-benchmark is not a re-decision authority for it. Where this study's receipts support the candidate under the permanent workload, that document is amended at its source with the new evidence rather than silently contradicted.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A findings document states a go or no-go verdict for each of $\mathbb{F}_3$, $\mathbb{F}_5$, and $\mathbb{F}_7$, each supported by a citation to a committed receipt.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each verdict states the measured crossover condition against the best applicable in-tree CPU path, or states explicitly that no crossover was observed within the measured range.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document specifies the intra-matrix parallel Ryser decomposition the study exercised — the per-lane Gray interval, the per-lane accumulator initialization, the lane-local row-product reduction, and the cross-lane partial-sum reduction — and links the executable prototype implementing it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The document explains why the $\mathbb{F}_3$ Boolean representation is valid for a permanent over $\mathbb{F}_3$ without treating an odd-characteristic permanent as a permanent over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
- [hard] REQ-05: For each of $\mathbb{F}_5$ and $\mathbb{F}_7$, the document reports at least two measured arithmetic representations before selecting or rejecting a design, citing the receipt for each.
- [hard] REQ-06: Every go verdict carries a production design covering input layout; persistent device buffers and streams named as the existing `DeviceBuffer`, `HipStreamPool`, and `LaunchDims` types in `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/`; bounded-duration launches; per-device initialization; error propagation that selects a tested CPU fallback for unsupported capabilities and recoverable resource failures while leaving fatal device failures explicit; and behavioral-equivalence coverage.
- [hard] REQ-07: The document names the public packed-field representation and the permanent-specialized internal state as distinct surfaces, chooses one of the two compliant resolutions described in the background, and, where the internal state is chosen, records the named exception together with its tracked convergence condition.
- [hard] REQ-08: Where the study's receipts support the three-plane $\mathbb{F}_7$ candidate, the archived $\mathbb{F}_7$ encoding decision document is amended at its source with the permanent-workload evidence and the changed verdict; otherwise the findings document states that the archived decision stands and cites the measurement leaving it standing.
- [hard] REQ-09: Falsified hypotheses, rejected candidates, and censored measurements are recorded together with the evidence contradicting them rather than removed.
- [hard] REQ-10: Every quantitative claim in the document resolves to a committed receipt file or to an in-tree source location.

## Notes

The document consumes committed evidence and introduces no new measurement.

The archived encoding decision lives under `dev/archive/`, which is permanent repository content; amending it is a deliberate act that needs owner approval before it lands.

Device facts stated in the findings are the receipted ones. Where an in-tree comment disagrees with a receipt — for example a compute-unit count recorded in a test file — the receipt governs and the stale comment is corrected in the same change.

The $\mathbb{F}_3$ arithmetic background is [Scheinerman2024].
